implementation_notes: Modern C++ default when a wire format is involved: define free functions void to_json(json&, const T&) and void from_json(const json&, T&) in the mapped type's own namespace; nlohmann's default adl_serializer finds them by argument-dependent lookup, so the two representations never mention each other and no converter class is written. The generic class form (template <class From, class To> struct Converter holding two callables) is a direct translation of the classic structure and is still justified when the mapping targets something other than JSON or when one object must be injected and shared by several callers.
pitfalls: to_json/from_json must be declared in the namespace of the mapped type (or an enclosing one) or ADL will not find them and the library falls back to a generic, wrong mapping.
at()/get_to() throw on missing or wrongly typed fields; a tolerant read needs explicit contains()/value() handling rather than a blanket try/catch.
Both functions must be visible before first use in every translation unit that converts the type, otherwise different mappings are compiled into different TUs.

variants.name: std::to_chars / std::from_chars scalar pair (C++17)
variants.implementation_notes: For scalar to text mappings the standard library ships a symmetric, locale-independent pair in <charconv>: from_chars parses into a value, to_chars writes one, and both return a result object that must be checked. This is the allocation-free replacement for a hand-written converter when the representations are a number and its text form; there is no registry, so the pairing discipline stays with the caller.
pitfalls: from_chars neither skips leading whitespace nor accepts a leading plus sign, unlike strtod, so input must be trimmed before the call.
Ignoring the returned pointer lets trailing garbage pass; comparing it with the end of the input range is the only complete check.
Floating-point overloads arrived later than the integer ones; guard with __cpp_lib_to_chars if the toolchain matrix includes older standard libraries.
